title: Biophilic architecture and designs for mental well-being
review_question: To review the contribution of biophilic architecture and designs to the improved physical space for mental well-being.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Primary literature, including articles, archives, and essays highlighting biophilia, was examined using deconstructive discourse analysis.

findings.antecedent: Biophilic architecture and designs (incorporating natural elements into built environments)
findings.consequent: Improved physical space for mental well-being, fulfilling and fruitful lives
findings.quote: review the contribution of biophilic architecture and designs to the improved physical space for mental well-being.

findings.antecedent: Biophilic design (incorporating natural elements into built environments)
findings.consequent: Alleviation of stress, enhanced cognitive performance, increased productivity, improved emotional well-being, reduced mental tiredness, fostering innovation and clarity of thought, creative and positive thinking
findings.source: Abstract, Section 1, Section 2, Section 3, Section 4, Section 5
findings.quote: biophilic design... may enhance cognitive performance, lessen stress, and promote emotional well-being in man-made spaces.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to a biophilic indoor environment (e.g., plants, natural elements)
findings.consequent: Lower systolic blood pressure, lower diastolic blood pressure, reduced skin conductance, improved short-term memory, reduction in negative feelings, increase in pleasant emotions
findings.quote: Participants' blood pressure was shown to be lower when exposed to a biophilic indoor environment... improvement in short-term memory was 14%.
key_citations: Yin J, Zhu S, MacNaughton P, Allen J G, Spengler JD 2018 Building Environ. 132, 255-262.
Yin J 2019 Bringing Nature Indoors with Virtual Reality: Human Responses to Biophilic Design in Buildings, Doctoral dissertation (Harvard University).

findings.antecedent: Green coverage ratio in indoor environments
findings.consequent: Restorative impact on people's mental state, favorable effect on physiological brain processes
findings.quote: the percentage of green covering is either too low (0.2%) or too high (20%) to have a restorative impact on people's mental state [32].
key_citations: Lei Q, Yuan C, Lau SS Y 2021 J. Cleaner Production 324, 129168.

findings.antecedent: Biophilic cities/urban biophilic designs (integrating natural elements, fostering appreciation for nature)
findings.consequent: Increased city well-being and resilience, improved inhabitants' health, social cohesion, reduced exposure to climate change hazards, psychological renewal, improved performance, mood, and well-being in metropolitan settings
findings.quote: Biophilic design patterns were developed to increase city well-being and resilience long-term [10].

findings.antecedent: Biophilic design in specific settings (prisons, residential areas for the elderly, university campuses)
findings.consequent: Lower stress, enhanced mental health, cognitive functioning, learning, decreased recidivism (prisons); reduced loneliness, anxiety, sadness, improved mental health and well-being (elderly); support for students' well-being, ability to cope, self-worth, physical health (university)
findings.quote: Bringing more nature and natural components into a prison has been shown to lower stress, enhance inmates' mental health, cognitive functioning, and learning, decrease recidivism...

synthesis_conclusions: Biophilic architecture and designs, by integrating natural elements, significantly contribute to improved mental and physical well-being across various settings (urban, indoor, specific populations).
There is a growing recognition of the innate human need for connection with nature (biophilia) and its therapeutic potential for stress reduction, cognitive enhancement, and emotional well-being.
Urban planning should prioritize biophilic design to create resilient cities that foster human-nature interaction and mitigate the negative impacts of urbanization and climate change.
Specific design parameters, such as optimal greenery dosage (e.g., 12% green coverage), can maximize restorative effects.
evidence_gaps: Further research is required to determine the optimal greenery dosage and its associated well-being advantages for use in design practice.
More empirical and practical evaluation is required to fully investigate the effects of biophilic design patterns and frameworks.
More research is needed on the impact of biopsychosocial and biophilic design in urban higher education institutions.
Evidence for the health and productivity benefits of interior biophilic elements, while existing, is still limited and warrants further investigation.
Some pathways by which biophilic architecture increases resilience are more uncertain and warrant further research and discoveries.
limitations: The review employs deconstructive discourse analysis, which is not a systematic review protocol, potentially leading to selection bias or lack of quantitative synthesis.
The paper acknowledges that some identified pathways for biophilic architecture's benefits are 'more uncertain and warrant further research and discoveries'.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract:
Abstract
               There is a growing recognition that people who stay in contact with nature are more likely to enjoy fulfilling, fruitful lives. More recently, architects and designers have begun to recognize the importance of biophilic design, which incorporates natural elements into built environments. However, as urbanization spreads around the globe, attention must be redirected to city size, with an emphasis on planning for and making progress toward “biophilic cities.” Biophilic communities are ones that aim to foster a sense of appreciation and stewardship for the natural world among their citizens by providing them with enough opportunities to experience nature both inside and beyond the city limits. Employing deconstructive discourse analysis on different uses of biophilic concepts, the present paper aims to review the contribution of biophilic architecture and designs to the improved physical space for mental well-being.
